content:
You are going to struggle to find most things if you can not find the help entry on the application menu.

Or perhaps you need to get back to the traditional menu system. I certainly prefer it.

If so right click beside the search box on the top bar and select menu bar.

Now to the results of the last images you posted.

The fundamental problem here is you have a server name indicating POP, but the account type is IMAP. That is not going to work and to be honest probably never should have, pop.shaw.ca resolves to pop.glb.shawcable.net [64.59.136.142]

imap.shaw.ca resolves to imap.glb.shawcable.net [64.59.136.142]

That the two server names resolve to the same IP address might mean the server is deciding the protocol it "speaks" based on the port you connect from. Port 993 is the default port for IMAP using SSL/TLS

That it is not working for you might indicate that some sort of prefiltering is happening at the cluster level, so try changing the server name to the one provided on the [https://www.rogers.com/support/internet/shaw-email/pop-and-imap-email-server-settings#imap-with-ssl-tls rogers website. ]

Incoming Mail Server Information: Incoming Mail Server: imap.shaw.ca Incoming Port: 993 SSL/TLS: Yes Username: Shaw email address without the @shaw.ca Password: Your email password

Outgoing Mail Server Information: Outgoing Mail Server: mail.shaw.ca Outgoing Port: 587 SSL/TLS: Yes Username: Shaw email address without the @shaw.ca Password: Your email password

While you make no statement about your outgoing server specifically, I notice that you have it configured to use STARTTLS. but Rogers suggest only using SSL/TLS. As both offer similar levels of encrypted communication I would suggest sticking with what your provider suggests, sure STARTTLS offers a little more security, but most of the world functions fine with just TLS (SSL being it's predecessor and actually not supported by default in Thunderbird, despite the list entry indicating otherwise.)
